CITY COUNCIL OF MONTEREY PARK
AND THE CITY COUNCIL ACTING ON BEHALF OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY OF THE FORMER
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
  AGENDA

  REGULAR MEETING
  Monterey Park City Hall Council Chambers
  320 W. Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754

  Wednesday
  August 7, 2019
  7:00 p.m.
  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services
  to enhance the quality of life for our entire community.

Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located at
320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and the City’s
website at www.montereypark.ca.gov.
PUBLIC COMMENTS ON AGENDA ITEMS
You may speak up to 5 minutes on Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time with
another person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor and City
Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers.
Per the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting
please call City Hall at (626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours before a
meeting. Council Chambers are wheelchair accessible.
This Agenda includes items considered by the City Council acting on behalf of the Successor Agency
of the former Monterey Park Redevelopment Agency which dissolved February 1, 2012. Successor
Agency matters will include the notation of “SA” next to the Agenda Item Number.

CALL TO ORDER  Mayor
FLAG SALUTE  The Monterey Park Fire Explorers
ROLL CALL  Peter Chan, Mitchell Ing, Stephen Lam, Hans Liang, Teresa Real Sebastian

AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS. While all comments are welcome, the Brown Act does not allow the City
Council to take action on any item not on the agenda. The Council may briefly respond to comments
after Public Communications is closed. Persons may, in addition to any other matter within the City
Council's subject-matter jurisdiction, comment on Agenda Items at this time. If you provide public
comment on a specific Agenda item at this time, however, you cannot later provide comments at the
time the Agenda Item is considered.

2-A.  UPDATE ON EMERGENCY REPAIR/REPLACEMENT OF SEWER MAIN AND WATER MAIN
  IN ALLEY EAST OF ATLANTIC BLVD BETWEEN EL MERCADO AVENUE AND EL
  PORTAL PLACE
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1)  Receiving and filing this update on the status of ongoing emergency replacement of the
  sewer and water mains along the alley east of Atlantic Boulevard between El Mercado
  and El Portal;
  (2)  Ending the emergency approved by Resolution No. 12088 and authorizing the City
  Manager to memorialize that conclusion; and
  (3) Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The emergency and extended repairs are categorically exempt from the requirements of the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to 14 California Code of Regulations §
  15269 (emergency repair to this public facility is necessary to maintain service essential to the
  public, health and welfare) and § 15301 (Existing Facilities). The extended repairs would result in
  minor alterations to existing public facilities involving no significant expansion of the existing use.
  The project is not anticipated to have any significant impacts with regard to traffic, noise, air
  quality, or water quality. There are adequate utilities and public services to serve the project.

[3.]  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS NOS. 3A-3I

3-A.  WARRANT REGISTER FOR THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK OF JULY 17 AND
  AUGUST 7, 2019
  It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Approve payment of warrants and adopt a Resolution allowing certain claims and
  demands per Warrant Register dated July 17 and August 7, 2019 totaling $1,758,080.84
  specifying the funds out of which the same are to be paid; and
  (2) Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

3-B.  MONTHLY INVESTMENT REPORT – JUNE 2019
  It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Receive and file the monthly investment report; and
  (2) Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

3-C.  IDENTIFYING A TAX RATE FOR COLLECTING VOTER AUTHORIZED PROPERTY TAXES
  FOR EMPLOYEE RETIREMENT BENEFITS BASED ON THE ASSESSED VALUATION
  ESTABLISHED BY THE COUNTY ASSESSOR’S OFFICE
  It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Adopt a Resolution identifying the amount of tax revenue required to fulfill the voters’
  intent in funding the City’s retirement system; and
  (2) Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

3-D.  MINUTES
  It is recommended that the City Council and the City Council acting on behalf of the Successor
  Agency:
  (1)  Approve the minutes from the regular meetings of June 5 & 19, 2019 and the special
  meetings of May 29, June 5 & June 19, 2019; and
  (2)  Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

3-E.  PURCHASE AND CONVERSION OF TWO, 2020 FORD UTILITY POLICE INTERCEPTOR
  SUVS
  It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1)  Waive bidding requirements pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code § 3.20.050(5) and
  authorize the City Manager to amend the contract (Agreement # 1967-A) with Wondries
  Fleet Group, in a form approved by the City Attorney, for the purchase of two, 2020 Ford
  Utility Police Interceptor SUVs through Wondries Fleet Group;
  (2)  Authorize the City Manager to amend the contract (Agreement 1967-AC) with West Coast
  Lights and Siren, in a form approved by the City Attorney, for the conversion/up-fitting of
  two 2020 Ford Utility Police Interceptor SUVs through West Coast Lights and Siren; and
  (3)  Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

3-F.  PRESIDIO NETWORKED SOLUTIONS GROUP, LLC. – APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1)  Authorizing the City Manager to execute a one year agreement, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney, with Presidio Networked Solutions Group, LLC for an amount not to exceed
  $69,742.45, for Verdugo Fire Emergency Communication System Upgrade, based on
  MPMC § 3.20.050 (5); and
  (2)  Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

3-G.  FIREFIGHTER UNIFORMS PURCHASE – APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1)  Authorizing the City Manager to execute an agreement, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney, with to Tom’s Clothing & Uniforms for an amount not to exceed $51,106 per
  fiscal year, for the purchase of firefighter uniforms; and
  (2)  Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK AND NEOGOV
  It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1)  Authorize the City Manager to execute a Renewal Agreement, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney, with NEOGOV for a human resources information system; and
  (2)  Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

3-I.  CONSIDERATION AND POSSIBLE ACTION TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION OF INTENT TO
  AMEND THE CITY’S CALPERS CONTRACT CAUSING MEMBERS OF THE MONTEREY
  PARK POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION (“POA”) TO MAKE ADDITIONAL PAYMENTS
  TOWARD CALPERS COST AS FOLLOWS: AN ADDITIONAL 3% BY CLASSIC
  EMPLOYEES; AND 0.5% FOR PEPRA EMPLOYEES. THE PROPOSED ACTION INCLUDES
  INTRODUCING AN ORDINANCE THAT, IF ADOPTED, WOULD AMEND THE CALPERS
  CONTRACT

  (1)  Adopting a Resolution providing notice of an intent to amend the City’s CalPERS contract
  to increase contributions made by POA members to CalPERS retirement costs;
  (2)  Adopting a Resolution providing notice of an intent to amend the City’s CalPERS contract
  to increase contributions made by POA members to CalPERS retirement costs;
  (3)  Authorize the City Clerk to sign the “Certificate of Compliance with Government Code
  Section 7507”; and
  (4)  Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

[4.]  PUBLIC HEARING

4-A.  A PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER THE ADOPTION OF THE 2019-2020 ANNUAL ACTION
  PLAN AS REQUIRED BY THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) AND
  HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIP ACT (HOME) PROGRAMS
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1)  Opening the public hearing to receive testimonial and documentary evidence;
  (2)  Adopting the One Year Action Plan for Program Year 2019-2020 and authorize the City
  Manager to implement the adopted Action Plan including, without limitation, to execute
  appropriate agreements in a form approved by the City Attorney; and
  (3)  Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

4-B.  PUBLIC HEARING - CONSIDERATION OF COSTS RESULTING FROM ABATING WEED
  NUISANCES AND AUTHORIZING COLLECTION VIA TAX ROLL
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  (1) Opening the public hearing to receive verbal and documentary testimony regarding
  nuisance abatement costs;
  (2) Adopting a resolution approving Weed Abatement Clearance Charge List and authorizing
  collection of such costs through the property tax rolls; and
  (3) Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  (1)  Discuss and consider joining a Joint Powers of Authority (JPA) – Transit Corridor Agency
  – with the cities of El Monte, Industry, Montebello, Rosemead, and South El Monte;
  (2)  Authorize the City Manager to enter into a JPA agreement with the cities of El Monte,
  Industry, Montebello, Rosemead, and South El Monte, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney, and authorize the City Manager to appropriate $25,000 in Measure M and/or
  Measure R funds to fund the membership contributions; and
  (3)  Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

5-B.  LIBRARY ANNUAL REPORT TO COUNCIL FROM THE LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES

TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
FROM:  Mark A. McAvoy, Director of Public Works/City Engineer
SUBJECT:  Update on Emergency Repair/Replacement of Sewer Main and Water
  Main in Alley East of Atlantic Blvd between El Mercado Avenue and El
  Portal Place

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Receiving and filing this update on the status of ongoing emergency replacement
  of the sewer and water mains along the alley east of Atlantic Boulevard between
  El Mercado and El Portal;
  2. Ending the emergency approved by Resolution No. 12088 and authorizing the City
  Manager to memorialize that conclusion; and
  3. Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

CEQA (California Environmental Qualitv Actl:

The emergency and extended repairs are categorically exempt from the requirements of
the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to 14 California Code of
Regulations S 15269 (emergency repair to this public facility is necessary to maintain
service essential to the public, health and welfare) and S 15301 (Existing Facilities). The
extended repairs would result in minor alterations to existing public facilities involving no
significant expansion of the existing use. The project is not anticipated to have any
significant impacts with regard to traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality. There are
adequate utilities and public services to serve the project.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

On or about June 12, 2019, a sewer main collapse blocked sewer flows from being
conveyed along the subject alley. Temporary pumping operations were set up to keep
local businesses and residents in service while staff met with several contractors to
obtain bids to perform emergency sewer and water main repairs or replacement.

On June 19,2019 the City Council adopted Resolution No. 12088 declaring an
emergency and authorizing contracting without the need for bidding pursuant to Public
Contract Code. The City Council also authorized the City Manager to execute public
works contracts with qualified contractors for the required repairs and appropriate funds
from the Sewer and Water Capital accounts. Staff received three bids each for

  Page 6 of 532
 Staff Report
August 7,2019
Page 2 of 3

replacement of the sewer main and replacement of the water main and selected the
lowest bids. Additionally, staff requested a proposal to create record drawings to
memorialize both the sewer and water main installation from our sewer/water on-call
design consultant.

To date the sewer main and associated work has been completed, with only minor details
remaining in order to complete the record drawings. At the time this report was written,
the water main was being constructed and was approximately 50% complete. lt is
expected that all major work to complete the water main will be finished by the date of
this Council meeting; again, with only minor details remaining.

BACKGROUND:

As presented at the June 19, 2019 City Council meeting an 8-inch cement concrete
sewer main, built in 1933, collapsed in several areas within the alley east of S Atlantic
Blvd between El Mercado Avenue and El Portal Place. ln addition to the age of the sewer
main, multiple water leaks from the adjacent 4-inch cast iron water main may have
caused the sewer collapse or compounded the issues. lt was determined that
replacement of both mains was required and staff sought out quotes from at least five
contractors who visited the site. As mentioned above staff received three bids for each
the sewer main replacement and the water main replacement.

The sewer replacement bids were as follows

Vasilj, lnc. was selected for construction of the sewer main and trench repair and they
have completed all construction work with only minor details, as mentioned above,
remaining. Doreck Construction was selected for replacement of the water main and
should have completed a majority of the work by time of this meeting. SA Associates will
be preparing as-built or record drawings to memorialize these improvements at a cost not
to exceed $11,000.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

A wastewater main collapse occurring on or about June 12, 2019 blocked wastewater
flows from being conveyed. Currently, temporary pumping operations have been set up

contractors to obtain bids to perform emergency wastewater and water main repairs or

replacement to reestablish wastewater flows and eliminate water leaks, which compound
the wastewater issues.

-B'ASKGEoUND:

On or about June 12, 2019 an 8-inch cement concrete wastewater main, built in 1933,
collapsed in several areas within the alley east of South Atlantic Blvd between El
Mercado Avenue and El Portal Place. ln addition to the age of the wastewater main,
multiple water leaks from the adjacent 4-inch cast iron water main may have caused the
wastewater collapse or compounded the issues. Currently, wastewater flows are being
blocked and therefore temporary bypass of the flows are occurring through the operation
of two pumps, in order to keep over 20 businesses, such as several restaurants, and
residents with wastewater service.

Additionally, the wastewater main collapse and water main leaks resulted in extensive
infrastructure damage besides the mains themselves such as the underlying alley
roadway bed, which could potentially lead to sink holes. The alley serves as the main
access for deliveries to the businesses served by these wastewater and water mains and
it is therefore important that it is structurally sound.

The City does not yet have a firm dollar figure or contractor for this project. While it is an
emergency, and the City caused temporary measures to be installed to ensure continued
wastewater service pending e permanent solution, the City is seeking the lowest dollar
figure with the best contractor. The Engineer's estimate for this project is in the $500,000
range; there are approximately 600-750 linear that must be excavated and constructed.

There are current discussions with four different qualified contractors for this work. The
City will select the best contractor for the lowest price; work is anticipated to begin next
week.

FISCAL IMPACT:

The Project will be paid for using funds from the Wastewater and Capital funds and staff
will update City Councilas soon as contract has been awarded.

  c.  Conditions of extreme peril to the safeÇ of persons and property arose on
  or about June 12, 2019 as a result of a 8-inch cement concrete
  wastewater main (built in 1933) collapsing in several areas within the alley
  east of South Atlantic Blvd between the intersections of El Portal Drive
  and El Mercado Avenue, and an adjacent 4-inch cast iron water main
  having multiple leaks in the same vicinity, compounding the wastewater
  main collapse.

  D  That collapsed wastewater main and water main leaks resulted in
  extensive infrastructure damage to the asphalt roadway and supporting
  roadway bed, the inability of wastewater flows to be conveyed without
  extensive pumping operations, temporary water and wastewater main pipe
  repairs, and more permanent water and wastewater main pipe installation,
  to ensure continued wastewater and water service to approximately 20
  residences and businesses in the area (the "emergency").

  welfare, the Acting City Manager declared an administrative emergency
  and directed the Public Works Director to take immediate emergency
  action to temporarily restore wastewater flows, and initiate repairs of the

  Park Municipal Code ('MPMC") Chapter 2.52.

1946 and 1952. The tax rate is limited byAB13 notto exceed the rate imposed in the 1983-

assessed valuation. This is the same rate since 1983-84 and it is also the maximum rate
allowed by 4813.

retirement tax revenue, including secured and unsecured retirement property taxes, residual
distributions, and General Fund transfer. The voter authorized property tax pays for $7.4
million of this overall retirement cost amount. The remaining expenditures will be covered by
the City's General Fund and Retirement Fund reserve.

  Every 10 years, as mandated by the U.S. Constitution, the federal government
  undertakes a census of the U.S. population to determine the allocation of seats
  held by each state in the House of Representatives. The next federal census will
  begin on April 1,2020.

  ln addition to determining federal representation, the census is used to distribute
  federal funding to states and local governments. Federal funding to states is
  determined based on population counts. lmproper accounting of populations or
  "undercount" may lead to reduced allocation of resources in the years ahead.
  Program allocations that may be impacted include Community Development Block
  Grant (CDBG) program, Propositions A, C, M and R which support transportation
  services and street repairs, as well as funding for school programs and public
  safety to name a few. lt is therefore, critical to do everything possible to avoid any
  undercounting or other misrepresentation of the City's population.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved a public awareness outreach campaign
  for the 2020 Census and approved the allocation of $42,000 from the General
  Fund on Consent Calendar.

SUBJECT:  Purchase and Conversion of two, 2020 Ford Utility Police lnterceptor

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council:
  1. Waive bidding requirements pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code S
  3.20.050(5) and authorize the City Manager to amend the contract (Agreement #
  1967-A) with Wondries Fleet Group, in a form approved by the City Attorney, for
  the purchase of lt'to,2020 Ford Utility Police Interceptor SUV's through Wondries
  Fleet Group;
  2. Authorize the City Manager to amend the contract (Agreement 1967-AC) with
  West Coast Lights and Siren, in a form approved by the City Attorney, for the
  conversion/up-fitting of two 2020 Ford Utility Police lnterceptor SUV's through
  West Coast Lights and Siren; and
  3. Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
ETEGUTIVE SUMMARY:

The 2019-2020 budget includes $135,000.00 for the replacement and conversion/up-
fitting of two vehicles for the Problem Oriented Policing Team (POP) and the Mental
Health Evaluation Team (MET) of the Police Department. Staff researched optional
vehicles and determined the 2020 Ford Utility Police lnterceptor SUV is the best
replacement choice as this vehicle meets the Police Department's needs. As such, Staff
recommends the purchase of two 2020 Ford Utility Police lnterceptor SUV's.

BAGKGROUND:

The Police Department has utilized the Ford Crown Victoria Police lnterceptor sedan for
over 15 years. Currently the Police Department's POP Team and MET Team are
utilizing 2004 and 2005 model year Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptors. These two
vehicles have reached the end of their service life and are in need of replacement.
ln the past, the Police Department was able to re-use equipment such as emergency
lights, safety screens, prisoner cages, radios, weapons racks, etc. as older vehicles
were taken out of service and new ones were placed into service. Ford discontinued
production of the Crown Victoria Police lnterceptor sedan in 2011. Consequently, the

  Page 144 of 532
 Staff Report
August 7,2019
Page 2

Police Department must switch to a completely new vehicle which does not allow for the
re-use of the equipment listed above.

Ford's 2020 Utility Police lnterceptor SUV comes standard with a 3.3 liter V6 engine,
1O-speed automatic transmission, all wheel drive, air bags (including side curtain air
bags for occupant safety), as well as an anti-lock braking system. Ford provides their
Utility Police lnterceptor SUV's with a 5-year1100,000 mile power train warranty (major
engine and transmission components) and a 3-yearl36,000 mile bumper to bumper
warranty.

These vehicles are available through a joint purchase program generally for larger
agencies such as the State of California (C.H.P.) and Los Angeles County (Sheriffs).
Under joint purchase, participating agencies can acquire goods and services at the
lowest price possible through volume discount without repeating the bid process. Joint
Purchase is a permitted purchasing method per Monterey Park Municipal Code Section
3.20.050(5).

Sourcewell, a Special District of Government and Cooperative Purchasing Agency,
issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) for several vehicles including the 2020 Ford Utility
Police lnterceptor SUV. Several companies across the nation responded with bids.
Sourcewell rated the bidders in several key areas and determined that National Auto
Fleet Group was the lowest priced responsible bidder, and therefore issued the contract
to National Auto Fleet Group (Contract #120716 attached). Contract #120716 is valid
from 01/1 712017 through 0111712021 . The City of Monterey Park is currently a member
of Sourcewell, membership #39242.

Wondries Fleet Group is able to obtain 2020 Ford Utility Police lnterceptors through the
Sourcewell (National Auto Fleet Group) Master Vehicle Contract #120716, for
$36,969.38 per unit. The cost for two vehicles is $73,938.76. This price includes sales
tax, tire fee, and delivery. Delivery of vehicles is estimated at 90-120 days from order.

The Police Department has used two vendors in the past for the conversion of Police
Vehicles. Those vendors being West Coast Lights and Siren, and Black and White
Emergency Vehicles.

Black and White Emergency Vehicles advised they are too busy to take on any
additional business from the City of Monterey Park. West Coast Lights and Siren
provided an estimated conversion turnaround time of 34 weeks from dealer delivery.

West Coast Lights and Siren has been the Police Department's primary vendor for the
past 12-years due to the consistency of their installations, so that the equipment is
mounted and functions the same in every vehicle. West Coast Lights and Siren is also
the only conversion shop that does custom fabrications and has an "on-site" machine
shop and welder. Being able to provide this service drastically cuts down the "turn-
around" time when a vehicle is being converted and we don't have to deal with any

additional vendors for the fabrication of specialty items such as weapon racks or MDC
mounts.

West Coast Lights and Siren also provide a mobile tech service to make any repairs or
minor conversions to vehicles in the field, if needed. This service reduces the "down
time" of any vehicle, as well as the man hours, to transport that vehicle to the shop to be
repaired.

The cost of conversion/up-fitting of a 2020 Ford Utility Police lnterceptor SUV is
approximately $18,000.00 per vehicle. This price includes the purchase of new
equipment (push bars, consoles, cages, prisoner seats, emergency lights, electronic
controls, wiring etc.) that cannot be reused from the Ford Crown Victoria sedan as well
as the equipment that can be removed/reinstalled (two-way radios, in-car camera
system, Lojack, ALPR, etc). This price could vary slightly if we chose to add/change
items at the time of installation, or if items are found to be in need of repair.

The Police Department requests to use West Coast Lights and Siren as the conversion
vendor due to their availability, efficiency, and consistency of installations/conversions.

Vehicle under account #0362-801-4211-54060 and an additional $67,500 was budgeted
to replace the MET Team Vehicle under account #0060-801 -04211-54060.

BACKGROUND/ANALYSIS
Verdugo Fire Communications Center (Verdugo Fire) dispatches F¡re/EMS resources for
fourteen (14) agencies within Los Angeles County; inclusive of, thirteen (13) municipalities and
the Burbank-Hollywood Airport Fíre Department. Verdugo Fire seryes a resident population of

$121 billion dollars. Historically, the Center has handled up lo 10"/" of all emergency incident
volume in Los Angeles County. Annually, it processes over 156,000 phone calls, which results
in over 80,000 incidents per year.

For several years now, Verdugo Fire has been researching a number of viable alternatives for
the replacement of íts 3O-year-old Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) system. The CAD and
related mapping software a¡e two of the most critical pieces of a public-safety dispatch center's

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

In accordance with the Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Monterey
Park and the Monterey Park Firefighters Association, firefighters may obtain new
uniforms each fiscal year. ln preparation for the upcoming fiscal year, staff recently
solicited bids for the purchase of firefighter uniforms and accessories and seeks City
Council approvalto award a contract to Tom's Clothing & Uniforms.

BACKGROUND:

Each fiscal year, the firefighters are provided a $806 uniform allowance to purchase
new uniforms as provided in the current Memorandum of Understanding. The uniforms
worn by the Firefighters and Reserve Firefighters are made of a fire resistant material
called "Nomex." This material has excellent thermal, chemical, and radiation resistance
It is best known as a barrier to fire and heat.

On July 18,2018, staff received approval during the City Council Meeting to execute a
multi-year agreement with bidder, Uniform Headquarters, lnc. DBA Keystone Uniform
Depot ("Keystone"), for the purchase of firefighter uniforms for Fiscal Year 2018-2019.
During Fiscal Year 2018-2019, upon further communications with representatives from
Keystone, Keystone prices were higher than other vendors in the area when pricing for
multiple individual staff orders for Monterey Park Fire Department. The Keystone
uniform process did not fit the needs and budget of the Fire Department.

Staff recently conducted a bid based on the most commonly purchased uniform attire
and accessories (Price Sheet Comparison attached as Attachment 1). Galls, LLC

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

On March 4,2015, City Council approved a contract with NEOGOV to provide a Human
Resources lnformation System (HRIS). The benefits from having the NEOGOV software

NEOGOV fonruarded a renewal agreement that amends the term of the agreement to a

BACKGROUND:

the advertisement of available jobs, applicant input, applicant notifications, scheduling
for testing, and candidate tracking throughout the recruitment process. lt has also
automated the City's employee performance evaluation process and tracking system.

SUBJECT:  Authorize the City Manager to execute an Agreement Between the City

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney, with NEOGOV; and
  2. Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

During the Mid-Year Budget Presentation on February 4, 2015, the City Council
approved the funds for Human Resources to purchase a Human Resources lnformation
System (HRIS) and NEOGOV was the referenced system.

An agreement with NEOGOV will provide the City with a company that's well-
established in providing human resources information system software for the public
sector. These services will automate the current manual paper system including hiring,
on-boarding, and the performance evaluation process. NEOGOV is specifically
designed for the unique needs of public sector agencies. The benefits anticipated with
NEOGOV's software will be improved productivity and increased accountability.

Using NEOGOV, Human Resources will convert its current employee index card and
employment application systems to more of a paperless process. This will eliminate the
current process of staff manually entering employee information and over 1,000
employment applications annually into the current DOS software system, making HR
more efficient.

BACKGROUND:

The Human Resources Department has surveyed and researched many Human
Resources lnformation Systems (HRIS) for the past three years. The top three
competitors that stood out were CivicPlus, GRM Document Management and
NEOGOV.

  Page 216 of 532
 Staff Report
Page 2

CivicPlus is an expert in local government website design, development, and content
management. Many cities use CivicPlus for their government website design including
the City of Monterey Park. After meeting with a CivicPlus representative in October
2013, regarding its HRIS, Human Resources concluded that the CivicPlus HRIS was
too new and unknown as a product to consider purchasing.

GRM Document Management (GRM) is a leading provider of information management
solutions, well known for their file tracking and file keeping. The City Clerk's department
is currently using GRM to manage and maintain its files (Agenda, Minutes, Staff
Reports, Resolutions and more). Human Resources met with GRM regarding its Human
Resources component and it did not have an HRIS where employee data could be input
into the system and its Human Resources component could not assist with recruitment
or appraisal tracking.

NEOGOV is a well known Human Resources lnformation System in the public sector
and considered the "go to" system. Currently, 1,300 public agencies across the country
use NEOGOV. ln a survey of HR Departments in the greater Los Angeles County area,
staff found that 13 agencies still used a manual paper system, 18 agencies used
NEOGOV, three used civic plus and the other three use lesser known systems (see
Attachment 1). NEOGOV has all the components that Human Resources is looking for
and need that will improve productivity and efficiency.

The purchase will include the following four products

  1) lnsight Enterprise Edition (Recruitment, Applicant Application and Tracking
  System)

  2) Assist with Recruitment Advertising through Governmentjobs.com Job Posting
  Subscriptíon

  3) New Hire "Onboard" Processing system
  4) Perform (Performance Appraisal Tracking for all 450 employees)
The current system used to track applicants by the City is an outdated DOS based
operating system called SIGMA (see Attachment 2). SIGMA has been used since 1999
and it's reached its capacity. The program has been running into many problems and
since it is a DOS based software (not MS-Windows), the City is no longer able to install
it on new replacement computers.

The product that would replace SIGMA is called lnsight. lnsight will be used for the
recruitment and hiring process. lt is considered a comprehensive automated applicant
tracking solution. The lnsight system is web-based and will integrate with the City's
current website.

  Page 217 of 532
 Staff Report
Page 3

Another product included in the purchase is a job posting subscription to
Governmentjobs.com. This subscription is for unlimited job postings and advertisements
on Governmentjobs.com. GovernmentJobs.com is the largest, most comprehensive
career search engine for the public sector and will help us reach the most qualified and
skilled employees for the City.

The Onboard program includes onboarding software that will streamline the new hire
paper work, processes and training. Onboard will enable new hires to choose benefits,
review policies and procedures and complete 19 and W4 forms as well as sign forms,
allowing them to complete their new hire checklist online prior to their start date. This
time consuming process is currently done in person with one of the HR staff.

"Perform" automates the annual and probationary employee appraisals and optimizes
employee development allowing for the measurement of competencies and goals and
the development of succession plans. Again, this process is current tracked manually.

Perform and Onboard will effectively create a centralized system for employee tracking
and will contain the information currently being kept on the 3 x 5 index cards (see
Attachment 2). This will be a labor intensive transition for HR staff, but once the data
entry is completed, the NEOGOV system will be a tremendous asset for expediting HR
services.

NEOGOV offers many advantages to the City as well as its users. ln partnering with
NEOGOV, the City would promote its success by becoming more strategic and efficient
in HR processes.

The purchase of NËOGOV is consistent with the organizational goals of the City of
Monterey Park and will promote greater accountability and productivity for the Human
Resources Department. NEOGOV is most suitable to the needs of the City.

FISCAL IMPACT:

The fees for NEOGOV will be a one-time cost of $34,160, funded by the Technofogy
Fund and a recurring annual fee of $24,160 which will be funded through various funds
through the budget process.

RECOMMENDATION:

  retirement costs;

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

The 201 8-2022 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the City and Monterey
Park Police Officers'Association includes an agreement that the City amend the
CaIPERS contract to increase the contribution by POA members toward retirement
costs. That amendment would result in POA members increasing their own
contributions as follows: a 3% increase for classic employees and 0.5% for PEPRA
employees.

BACKGROUND:

On March 20,2019, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 12065 which approved the
MOU with POA for contract year 2018-2022. For CaIPERS cost sharing purposes, this
is governed by Government Code S 20516 which requires an amendment to the City's
CaIPERS contract.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development provides funding to states,
counties and cities in the form of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and
Home lnvestment Partnerships (HOME) funds. Since the City of Monterey Park is an
Entitlement City, the City is eligible to receive both CDBG and HOME funds which it has
for many years.

Before Monterey Park can receive these entitlement funds, federal regulations require
that a Consolidated Plan (i.e., five year plan) be adopted by the City that serves as the
federal planning document for those jurisdictions receiving Community Development
Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME lnvestment Partnerships (HOME) Program funds. The
Consolidated Plan was adopted by the City Council in 2015. ln addition, federal
regulations also require the adoption of an Annual Action Plan to the Consolidated Plan
that operates on a single program year established by the City (i.e., July 1 , 2019
through June 30, 2020). As required by federal requirements, the City will submit its
One Year Annual Action Plan to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban
Development (HUD) after today's meeting. The statutory submittal deadline for the
Annual Action Plan is August 16,2019.

The City of Monterey Park views the Annual Action Plan requirements as an opportunity
to reassess its housing needs and priorities, as well as its programs and resources in a
manner that will best meet the affordable housing and community development

TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
FROM:  Scott Haberle, Fire Chief
SUBJECT:  Public Hearing - Consideration of Costs Resulting from Abating Weed
  Nuisances and Authorizing Collection via Tax Roll

REGOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1) Opening the public hearing to receive verbal and documentary testimony
  regarding nuisance abatement costs;
  2) Adopting a resolution approving Weed Abatement Clearance Charge List and
  authorizing collection of such costs through the property tax rolls; and
  3) Taking such additional, related, action may be desirable.
EXEGUTIVE SUMMARY:
On February 6, 2019, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 12059 declaring that
weeds growing upon and in front of certain properties in the City are public nuisances
and directing that the County abate such nuisances. On February 20, 2019, the City
Council held a protest hearing and subsequently approved the Weed Abatement
Declaration List as posted by the County.

The County of Los Angeles Department of Agriculture Commissioner and Weights and
Measures submitted the annual Weed Abatement Charge List to the City of Monterey
Park for abating noxious or dangerous weeds and rubbish. Confirmation of the List by
the City Council will authorize the Agricultural CommissionAffeights and Measure to
place abatement costs resulting from the County's efforts onto the tax roll. lt should be
noted that these charges are from work performed by the County of Los Angeles during
Fiscal Year 2018-2019.

The County mailed notices before February 7,2019 to the record owner of each parcel
included in the declaration líst declaring that their parcel is an existing, future or
"potential" hazard. The County advised the owners that it considered a parcel a future
or potential hazard if the parcel is not completely landscaped or irrigated and there is a
potential for weed growth.

The County originally identified 1571 improved and unimproved parcels in the City as
public nuisances. The County advised the City that March 21,2019 was the last day the
City could request or the County authorize removal of a parcel from the list. Of these
1571 parcels, 1519 are the only ones being charged, 15'10 parcels will be charged the
annual inspection fee of $42.37 as established by the County Board of Supervisors. For

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council:
  1. Discuss and consider joining a Joint Powers of Authority (JPA) - Transit Corridor
  Agency - with the cities of El Monte, lndustry, Montebello, Rosemead, and South
  El Monte;
  2. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a JPA agreement with the cities of El
  Monte, lndustry, Montebello, Rosemead, and South El Monte, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney, and authorize the City Manager to appropriate $25,000 in
  Measure M and/or Measure R funds to fund the membership contributions;and
  3. Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

This report includes updates to existing discussion amongst the cities of El Monte,
lndustry, Montebello, Monterey Park, Rosemead, and South El Monte forming a JPA in
light of the transportation challenges directly related to the 710 freeway, 10 freeway, 60
freeway, and 605 freeway that affect these cities' major corridors.

BACKGROUND

On March 25,2019, the City of Rosemead hosted a Metro presentation regarding the
study of a Light Rail Transit alternative to extend the existing Metro Gold Line Eastside
Transit Corridor from its current terminus at Atlantic Station in East Los Angeles into
eastern Los Angeles County. Based on Metro's findings in its Technical Study, the
Board approved the following Updated Project Definition to include three Build
Alternatives:

  1. SR 60 NSDV LRT Alternative
  2. Washington Boulevard LRT Alternative - Atlantic Below-Grade Concept
  3. A Combined Concept
After the presentation, officials representing the cities of lndustry, Monterey Park, South
El Monte, and Rosemead had a discussion leading to the possibility of forming a JPA

regarding these future transportation challenges, which directly related to the 10,
freeway, 60 freeway, 605 freeway, and 710 freeway that affect these cities' major
corridors. A JPA will conduct all business on behalf of the Authority and will advocate for
the sub-region, join resources together to co-fund projects, and seek State and Federal
funding as a Joint Power.

At the June 1 1, 2019 Rosemead City Council meeting, the Rosemead City Council
approved the formation and particlpation in a JPA with the cities of El Monte, lndustry,
Montebello, Monterey Park, and South El Monte. A $25,000 appropriation was
approved to fund the portion of the City's contributions to this new JPA. Staff
recommends the City Council provide further direction of having the City of Monterey
Park joining the JPA.

FISCAL IMPACT:

Funding contributions in the amount of $25,000 from the cities of El Monte, lndustry,
Montebello, Monterey Park, Rosemead, and South El Monte will initially fund the start of
this new JPA. Measure R (Fund 0110) and/or Measure M (Fund 0112) funds may be
utilized to fund the City of Monterey Park's portion to join the JPA.

  On or about June 12,2019, a sewer main collapse blocked sewer flows from being
  conveyed along the subject alley. Temporary pumping operations were set up to
  keep local businesses and residents in service while staff met with several
  contractors to obtain bids to perform emergency sewer and water main repairs or
  replacement.

  emergency and authorizing contracting without the need for bidding pursuant to
  Public Contract Code. The City Council also authorized the City Manager to
  execute public works contracts with qualified contractors for the required repairs
  and appropriate funds from the Sewer and Water Capital accounts. Staff received
  three bids each for replacement of the sewer main and replacement of the water
  main and selected the lowest bids. Additionally, staff requested a proposal to
  create record drawings to memorialize both the sewer and water main installation
  from our sewer/water on-call design consultant.

  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) AND HOME INVESTMENT
  PARTNERSHIP ACT (HOME) PROGRAMS

  The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development provides funding to
  states, counties and cities in the form of Community Development Block Grant
  (CDBG) and Home lnvestment Partnerships (HOME) funds. Since the City of
  Monterey Park is an Entitlement City, the City is eligible to receive both CDBG and
  HOME funds which it has for many years.
   67- 164
  August 7,2019

 Before Monterey Park can receive these entitlement funds, federal regulations
 require that a Consolidated Plan (i.e., five year plan) be adopted by the City that
 serves as the federal planning document for those jurisdictions receiving
 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME lnvestment
 Partnerships (HOME) Program funds. The Consolidated Plan was adopted by the
 City Council in 2015. ln addition, federal regulations also require the adoption of an
 Annual Action Plan to the Consolidated Plan that operates on a single program
 year established by the City (i.e., July 1,2019 through June 30,2020). As required
 by federal requirements, the City will submit its One Year Annual Action Plan to the
 U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) after today's meeting.
 The statutory submittal deadline for the Annual Action Plan is August 16,2019.

 The City of Monterey Park views the Annual Action Plan requirements as an
 opportunity to reassess its housing needs and priorities, as well as its programs
 and resources in a manner that will best meet the affordable housing and
 community development challenges of the Monterey Park community. The
 estimated City entitlement for FY 2019-20 is $671 ,312 in CDBG funding and
 $346,000 in HOME funding.

4B.. PUBLIC HEARING  .
  CONSTDERATION OF COSTS RESULTING FROM
  ABATING WEED NUISANCES AND AUTHORIZING COLLECTION VIA TAX
  ROLL

  On February 6, 2019, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 12059 declaring
  that weeds growing upon and in front of certain properties in the City are public
  nuisances and directing that the County abate such nuisances. On February 20,
  2019, the City Council held a protest hearing and subsequently approved the
  Weed Abatement Declaration List as posted by the County.

  The County of Los Angeles Department of Agriculture Commissioner and Weights
  and Measures submitted the annual Weed Abatement Charge List to the City of
  Monterey Park for abating noxious or dangerous weeds and rubbish. Confirmation
  of the List by the City Council will authorize the Agricultural CommissionAffeights
  and Measure to place abatement costs resulting from the County's efforts onto the
  tax roll. lt should be noted that these charges are from work performed by the
  County of Los Angeles during Fiscal Year 2018-2019.

  The County mailed notices before February 7, 2019 to the record owner of each
  parcel included in the declaration list declaring that their parcel is an existing,
  future or "potential" hazard The County advised the owners that it considered a
  parcel a future or potentialhazard if the parcel is not completely landscaped or
  irrigated and there is a potential for weed growth.

  The County originally identified 1571 improved and unimproved parcels in the City
  as public nuisances. The County advised the City that March 21,2019 was the last
  day the City could request or the County authorize removal of a parcel from the list.
  Of these 1571 parcels, 1519 are the only ones being charged, 1510 parcels will be
  charged the annual inspection fee of $42.37 as established by the County Board of
  Supervisors. For this previous year, there were nine parcels that required the
  County to perform weed abatement services. The nine parcels were charged a
  total of $12,705.02 that is reflected on the weed abatement charge list attached to
  the staff report.

  Action Taken: The City Council opened the public hearing to receive verbal and
  documentary testimony regarding nuisance abatement costs at 9:47 p.m., there
  being no speakers, closed the public hearing al954 p.m.; and adopted Resolution
  No. 12096 approving Weed Abatement Clearance Charge List and authorized
  collection of such costs through the property tax rolls.
